post.caption: A jeweler minted the first gold dollar. German goldsmith Christopher Bechtler reached North Carolina in 1830. He opened a shop that made jewelry and clocks. The nearest federal mint sat in Philadelphia, far from the mines. So he made his own dies and press, then struck gold coins. His first gold coins came out in the summer of 1831. A gold dollar followed, the first ever made in the United States. The federal Mint struck its own gold dollar only in 1849. Each coin carried his name and its weight in gold. A Bechtler five dollar coin dated 1834 is kept in the Smithsonian.
